MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  FEBRUARY 19, 2019

  An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates
  was called to order at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chamber at Rolling Hills Estates City Hall, 4045
  Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California by CHAIR ROMANELLI.

  2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  CHAIR ROMANELLI led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  COMMISSIONERS PRESENT:  McCormick, Pope, Persichina, Romanelli,
  Retz, Ciarolla, Bain

  COMMISSIONERS ABSENT:  None

  STAFF PRESENT:  Andy Clark, Community Services Director
  Alexa Davis, Assistant to the City Manager
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  4.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION REORGANIZATION

  Community Services Director Clark stated that the City Council appointed VICE CHAIR
  RETZ as CHAIR and Commissioner Persichina as VICE CHAIR.

  VICE CHAIR RETZ thanked CHAIR ROMANELLI for his service and leadership and
  presented him with a plaque.

  CHAIR ROMANELLI stated that it was an honor to serve in 2018 and look forward to
  working with the new commissioners in 2019.

  5.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES DECEMBER 17, 2018

  VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI
  to:
  APPROVE THE CORRECTED PARKS AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION
  MINUTES OF DECEMBER 17, 2018.

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

  6.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA
  None

  7.  CONSENT CALENDAR
  None

  8.  ADJOURN TO PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION ADVISORY BOARD MEETING

  VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER POPE to,

  ADJOURN TO THE PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION ADVISORY BOARD
  MEETING

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES,  1
FEBRUARY 19, 2019
   There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

  A.  PROPOSED NEW FOUNDATION LOGO

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis stated that staff has worked with the consulting firm,
  Tripepi Smith, on creating a new logo for the Pepper Tree Foundation. The proposed logo
  would be a better representation of what the foundation stands for and what it is
  supporting. The logo will be used for branding of events, the newsletter, and promotional
  materials.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis welcomed the commission’s input.

  COMMISSIONER POPE stated that the foundation also supports trail improvements and
  maintenance and suggested more indication of that and also representation of equestrian
  is needed.

  CHAIR RETZ stated that this is an equestrian community and it is important to include this
  in the logo and suggested removing the bench and replacing it with a horse and a rider.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK suggested adding people in the logo.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN suggested making the tree smaller and agreed with including a
  horse and a trail.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis stated that she will come back with another draft and
  stated that the City Council will be holding their Policy Development Session in March and
  a brainstorming idea is to review what the Pepper Tree Foundation is doing and what it
  could do. If discussed, it will be brought back to this commission for further input.

  B.  2019 HILLS ARE ALIVE RACE AGREEMENT

  Community Services Director Clark stated that this is the standard agreement with Michael
  Hogue. The $4,000 advanced management fee will remain the same as in all past years.
  This fee is used for him to secure sponsors, assists with promoting the race, and getting
  more runners to participate.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that staff recommends that the Pepper Tree
  Foundation Advisory Board make a recommendation to the Pepper Tree Foundation
  Board of Directors to approve the agreement with Michael Hogue Productions to provide
  fundraising, promotional and consulting services for the 2019 Hills Are Alive Race.

  In reference to Malaga Bank’s request in 2018 to sponsor all the city’s 2019 special events,
  VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA explained that any sponsorships obtained exclusively by the
  commissioner’s would be wholly for the city and would not be split with Michael Hogue
  Productions.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if this event raises funds above the $4,000 management
  fee. Community Services stated yes and that approximately $4,300, aside from the
  management fee, was raised last year.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if the participation rate was being tracked and if there is an
  expectation to grow that race. Community Services Director stated that the participation
  is being tracked and the participation rate for this event is steady while other area race
  numbers are dropping. Community Services Director Clark stated that there will also be
  about three Race Subcommittee meetings prior to the event where Michael Hogue will
  report on his activity.

  In response to a question by Anthony Campanella, Resident, Community Services
  Director Clark stated that the event is a Run and Walk Race.

  VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA
  to,

  MAKE A RECOMMENDATION TO THE PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION BOARD
  OF DIRECTORS TO APPROVE THE AGREEMENT WITH MICHAEL HOGUE
PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES,  2
FEBRUARY 19, 2019
   PRODUCTIONS TO PROVIDE FUNDRAISING, PROMOTIONAL  AND
  CONSULTING SERVICES FOR THE 2019 HILLS ARE ALIVE RACE.

  AYES:  McCormick, Pope, Persichina, Romanelli, Retz, Ciarolla, Bain
  NOES:
  ABSENT:
  ABSTAIN:

  VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA
  to,
  RECONVENE TO THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

  10.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  TABER GROVE PHASE II CONCEPTUAL PLAN

  Community Services Director Clark provided a summary of the staff report for this item.
  He stated that in May, the Park and Activities Commission went on a tour of the park and
  stated that there was interest in creating a scenic viewing area where the adjacent home
  is encroaching onto the city property. The new commissioners recently toured the park
  and also met with Mr. Campanella (owner of the adjacent property).

  Community Services Director Clark provided diagrams with several options to consider for
  the scenic viewing area.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that staff recommends that the Park and
  Activities Commission: 1) Determine the size of the proposed viewing area in Phase II of
  the Taber Grove development project; 2) Select the site amenities to be placed in the
  Phase II area of Taber Grove; and 3) Recommend to City Council that Pepper Tree
  Foundation funds be allocated to complete Phase II of the Taber Grove development
  project.

  CHAIR RETZ suggested signage at the George F. Canyon Nature Center to let visitors
  know that there is a scenic viewing area. Community Services Director stated that this
  would be appropriate, however, this is mostly a neighborhood park and not necessarily a
  destination park.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN stated that the plan contemplates additional fencing of the new
  developed area and suggested signage at Harbor Sight. COMMISSIONER BAIN added
  that the presence of the grove area should be part of the signage plan.

  A brief discussion ensued regarding signage.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that Mr. Campanella would like to apply for an
  encroachment permit for the portion of land which will not be used for this project.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN stated that she appreciated Mr. Campanella’s willingness to
  remove one or two of the fruit trees which may obscure the view, and further suggested
  to work around the trees since they are well established and have a lot of fruit.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked about the amount of area that Mr. Campanella
  would like to obtain an encroachment permit for. Mr. Campanella stated that it would be
  an amount within reason.

  Mr. Campanella expressed his concerns with being able to see kids from the grove to the
  proposed viewing area and also with safety at that corner.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN inquired about the timeline for the Taber Grove portion and asked
  about the piping, grading, drainage, and clean-up. Community Services Director Clark
  stated that the widening of the trail will also be part of the project. The City Council recently
  approved that master agreement with Wildan Engineering and currently they are working
  on the bid documents. The bid documents should be out within the next 30 days.
PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES,  3
FEBRUARY 19, 2019
   COMMISSIONER POPE stated that the idea to clean-up the grove portion and make it
  useable is very generous of Mr. Taber. In giving this more thought, COMMISSIONER
  POPE stated that she does not see the higher scenic view portion as usable space for
  families or park space anymore, specifically with the retaining wall that is there.

  CHAIR RETZ suggested tabling this until Phase I is complete and revisiting the site taking
  into consideration the three options that have been presented.
  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated that there may be a need to have a community
  meeting so they may provide some input on what they would like to see there. Community
  Services Director Clark stated that the HOA’s were notified of the meetings, but more
  outreach can be made by staff to residents and the HOA’s.

  Mr. Campanella stated that signage on Harbor Sight would not be a good idea because
  there is no parking on that street.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that a plaque is ready to be installed onto a
  boulder but there are no plans to place a City Park sign.

  The Park and Activities Commission agreed to table this item.

  B.  PROPOSED PARK REGULATION REVISIONS

  Community Services Director Clark stated that COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI and staff
  reviewed the park regulations and made needed changes.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that staff recommends that the Park and
  Activities Commission make a recommendation to City Council to amend Municipal Code
  Sections 12.24.020 and 12.24.050.

  In response to questions by COMMISSIONER BAIN, Community Services Director Clark
  stated that feather flags and balloons are prohibited due to the affect the noise has on the
  horses. Piñatas are prohibited due to the mess that they create.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked why structures and tents are not prohibited and if it would
  be easier to prohibit structures larger than 10’x10’. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI
  explained that there are city sponsored events use large canopies and rather than prohibit,
  just have applicant disclose what their event will include and staff can review and inform
  the applicant of any other requirements on a case by case basis.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN inquired about section 12.24.020 (D), when referring to prohibiting
  within the airspace over public parks within the city. COMMISSIONER RETZ stated that
  the airspace begins at one inch. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI added that the park is
  within 5 miles of an airport and the FAA requires that notification be made to the tower
  prior to launching anything into the airspace.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN suggested clarification in the last sentence in section 12.24.050
  – Animals.

  A discussion ensued to add animals, such as goats and pigs, to the list of permitted on
  leash animals in the park.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that the revisions will be brought back to the
  Commission.

  11.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK REPORTS

  COMMISSIONER BAIN stated that she visited Highridge Park and noted erosion on the
  trails and maintenance needed to the restroom structure. Community Services Director
  Clark stated that the park is on the list for grading and a plan for the entire restroom
  structure will be presented to the Commission in the near future.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES,  4
FEBRUARY 19, 2019
   COMMISSIONER MCCORMICH stated that the green canopy over the deck area at
  George F. Canyon Park is damaged. Community Services Director Clark noted this.

  B.  SOUTH BAY CITIES COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS GENERAL ASSEMBLY –
  FEBRUARY 28, 2019 – CHAIR RETZ announced that this event it coming up and
  encouraged the Commissioners to attend.

  C.  SHELTER FUNDAMENTALS TRAINING – MARCH 16, 2019 – Assistant to the City
  Manager Davis stated that in the case of an emergency, the City is required to open up a
  shelter, the Red Cross would typically take 72 hours to set-up a shelter. This is a good
  training opportunity for Commissioners.

  D.  FAIR POLITICAL PRACTICES COMMISSION FORM 700 DUE APRIL 1, 2019 – CHAIR
  RETZ reminded the Commissioners to submit Form 700 to the City Clerk by April 1st.

  9.  DIRECTOR’S ITEMS (Verbal Reports)

  A.  NATURE CENTER RE-DESIGN WORKSHOP – FEBRUARY 28, 2019 – Community
  Services Director Clark stated that the meeting will be held in the Council Chamber at 7:00
  p.m. All residents were notified by mail about the meeting.

  B.  COMMUNITY SERVICES DIRECTOR RETIREMENT – JUNE 13, 2019 – Community
  Services Director Clark announced that he will be retiring on June 13th. In response to a
  question by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI, Assistant to the City Manager Davis stated
  that a manager/supervisor will be hired, and two additional full-time people, which includes
  Mike Goldsmith who will take on more responsibility and Daniel A-Haja who will go
  from part-time to full-time.

  10.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF FEBRUARY 12, 2019

  B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF JANUARY 22, 2019

  C.  PLANNING COMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 4, 2019

  D.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE DRAFT MINUTES OF JANUARY 28, 2019

  E.  2018 PARADE OF LIGHTS DEBRIEFING REPORT

  RECEIVED AND FILED ITEMS 10A-10E

  11.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  RECREATION FEES REVIEW – Community Services Director stated that this item will be
  brought before the Park and Activities Commission at the next meeting.

  12.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR RETZ adjourned the meeting at 8:20 p.m.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  _____________________________
  Carol Corea  Heidi Luce
  Administrative Assistant  City Clerk

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES,  5
FEBRUARY 19, 2019
